svg.title: Downshift current runtime routing architecture
svg.desc: Diagram based on the Downshift main branch. Harness hooks feed adapters, which call core.Route, use catalog and session allowlists, plan a safe rewrite, then emit harness-specific steering. Telemetry and decision intelligence are side paths. Capability Router v2 and orchestration planner are implemented but outside the current hook main routing path.
svg.text: internal/core · deterministic · zero LLM calls · zero network
regex · lang guard · risk floors · nudges
catalog picks harness model for target tier
preserve/review intent; uncertain downgrade is gated
only writes a model that the current session actually exposes
operator-selected specialised models are never auto-replaced
uncertain classified downgrade is not blindly applied
classified ID, otherwise cheapest/strongest eligible session model
prefer same model family, switch effort when compatible
rewrite model/effort, allow unchanged, or KiroCrew respawn instruction
IDs · aliases · family · tier · cost · effort · explicit_only
IMPLEMENTED, OUTSIDE CURRENT HOOK MAIN PATH
13 signals → safety floor → softmax → risk policy → matcher
Model/provider agnostic; offline weights + capability-aware design.
Not the adapter runtime call today: adapters still invoke core.Route.
dedup → preserve order → max_delegates / capability cap
Does not infer subtasks and does not choose agent or model.
What actually happens on a subagent spawn
1. Harness emits its hook event → 2. adapter extracts the child task → 3. core.Route classifies and selects a tier/model from the catalog →
4. PlanForSession proves the target exists in that session and respects explicit/confidence gates → 5. adapter emits the harness-native rewrite.
Every failure path is fail-open: Downshift must not become an availability risk for the coding harness.
Source: github.com/tiagovilasboas/downshift-ai · main branch read 2026-09-30 · diagram reflects code, not roadmap claims.
